findings.assertion: The 20 August 1847 battle at Churubusco took place at the former convent now housing the Museo Nacional de las Intervenciones. INAH identifies Mexican military defenders and the Irish San Patricio Battalion in this confrontation.
findings.source_locator: INAH Lugares museum description; INAH museum Relevancia cultural
findings.limitations: Institutional summaries rather than contemporaneous orders or battle accounts; no inference about exact battlefield positions or surviving damage

findings.assertion: The Churubusco site combines preconquest Huitzilopochco, a Franciscan presence beginning in the sixteenth century and convent fabric containing seventeenth-century floors and wash features visible in museum archaeological exposures; the institution also describes an 1806 floor releveling.
findings.source_locator: INAH Lugares overview 'intersección de tres tiempos'; INAH Museo passage 'refectorio ... calas arqueológicas ... renivelación 1806'
findings.limitations: Historic building phases based on INAH institutional interpretation; individual architectural features and access route need on-site verification

findings.assertion: INAH records Benito Juárez's 1869 designation of the former Churubusco convent as a national monument and its later opening as the Museo Nacional de las Intervenciones on 13 September 1981. These are heritage and museum milestones, not dates of the original battle.
findings.source_locator: INAH Lugares, opening history paragraphs; INAH Museos, Relevancia cultural
findings.limitations: Juárez decree facsimile and 1981 museum founding records not examined; building access current conditions not checked

findings.assertion: The site named Molino del Rey had earlier milling functions associated, according to the INAH monument catalogue, with water from the Santa Fe and Tacubaya systems; the Molino del Rey battle took place on 8 September 1847. The surviving building should not be read as unchanged sixteenth-century fabric.
findings.source_locator: INAH catalog Información histórica, first two paragraphs; INAH Arqueología 56 published abstract
findings.limitations: Historic mill chronology and integrity are catalogue claims; original architectural surveys, cadastral maps and building access not verified

findings.assertion: A 2019 INAH archaeological-history study describes relocation of a Molino del Rey funerary battle monument in 1985 amid construction of Metro Line 7, an intermediate site in Chapultepec's second section, and a further relocation to the Los Pinos gardens in 2014.
findings.source_locator: López Camacho and Velásquez Monroy 2019, publisher abstract (Resumen)
findings.limitations: Abstract only; full movement chronology, exact current location and visitor sightline not verified; not license to map a current position

findings.assertion: INAH distinguishes artillery attacks on Chapultepec beginning 12 September 1847 from the assault on 13 September, and identifies the Mexican army, San Blas Battalion and approximately fifty Military College cadets among the defenders. The six commemorated cadets were not the only combatants.
findings.source_locator: INAH 'Defensa en tiempos de invasión', first and second battle paragraphs
findings.limitations: Institutional commemoration rather than original casualty rolls; figures and timing require independent research; legend of flag leap not established
